draft.title: Conflicting views on sustainability
card: Sustainable use means using an environment in a way that meets today's needs without harming its ability to meet future needs.
Communities, businesses and governments often disagree about what sustainable use looks like. Each group has different interests and priorities.
A common cause is cost. Protecting an environment can cost jobs or profits in the short term, such as when fishing or logging is limited.
The benefits of protection, such as healthy fish stocks or forests, often come later. So people who lose income now may oppose limits, while others support them.
draft.remember: Groups can disagree because protecting an environment may cost jobs or profits now, while the benefits come later.

a.q: Why do businesses and conservation groups often disagree about limits on using an environment?
opts: Limits can cost jobs or profits now, but benefits come later
Limits always stop a business from earning any income
Only conservation groups care about future generations
Governments have no say in how an environment is used
a.why: Protection can mean lost income in the short term, while benefits such as healthy forests come later. The option saying income stops completely is wrong, because the card says limits can cost jobs or profits, not remove all income.
a.clue: Think about when the costs and the benefits of protection arrive.

b.q: A council in Tasmania plans to limit the number of fishing boats in a bay to protect fish stocks. Which response best shows why some local people might oppose the plan?
opts: Boat owners fear lost income before fish stocks recover
Boat owners want the fish stocks to run out sooner
Boat owners think the bay has no value to the community
Boat owners believe fish stocks will recover without limits
b.why: Limits can cost jobs or profits in the short term, while the benefit of recovered stocks comes later. Opposing the plan does not mean people want the environment harmed, so the option about running out is wrong.
b.clue: Ask what the boat owners lose first, and when the benefit arrives.

a.best: Limits can cost jobs or profits now, but benefits come later

b.best: Boat owners fear lost income before fish stocks recover
also_right: Boat owners believe fish stocks will recover without limits

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is the only one with a hedge ('can'). Every wrong option uses an absolute ('always', 'Only', 'no say'), so a student can pick the answer by spotting the qualifier without knowing the idea. It is also slightly the longest.

In Tasmania, commercial and recreational fishing is managed by the state government (NRE Tas), not local councils. A council limiting the number of fishing boats in a bay is not realistic in Australia. Change it to 'The Tasmanian Government'.

'Boat owners believe fish stocks will recover without limits' is a real and defensible reason some local people oppose fishing limits, because they dispute the need for limits. The intended answer is the best fit to the card, but this distractor is not clearly wrong. Replace it with a clearly wrong option.
